challenges.title: Smile or greet someone
challenges.description: Offer a small smile or a friendly hello to someone when it feels appropriate, such as a neighbour, a cashier, or a classmate.
challenges.preparation: Pick a setting where a quick hello feels natural, like a shop or your building.
instructions: Notice someone nearby who seems approachable.
Make brief eye contact and smile, or say a simple hello.
Let it end there if that feels like enough. A small step still counts.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel in the moment, and how did the other person respond?
challenges.easierStep: Smile at someone from a distance, or say hello to a familiar face.

challenges.title: Send a friendly message to someone you know
challenges.description: Reach out with a short, low-pressure message to a friend, relative, or colleague.
challenges.preparation: Think of someone you would enjoy hearing from. You do not need a big reason to say hi.
instructions: Choose one person.
Write one or two friendly sentences, such as asking how their week is going.
Send it, then carry on with your day without waiting for a reply.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What was it like to send it, and did anything surprise you?
challenges.easierStep: Write the message but save it as a draft, or react kindly to something they posted.

challenges.title: Start a short conversation about a shared interest
challenges.description: Talk briefly with someone about something you both enjoy, like a show, a hobby, or a local place.
challenges.preparation: Think of one interest you share with a person you already know a little.
instructions: Choose a calm moment when they are not rushed.
Open with a simple comment or question about the interest.
Listen for something they say and ask one follow-up question.
Wrap up warmly whenever you like.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you learn about them, and what helped the conversation along?
challenges.easierStep: Send a short message about the shared interest instead of talking in person.

challenges.title: Introduce yourself to someone new in a suitable setting
challenges.description: At a class, event, or group where meeting people is expected, say hello and share your name.
challenges.preparation: Choose a setting where introductions are normal. Prepare a one-line introduction and one question.
instructions: Pick a moment when the person is not busy.
Say your name and one simple thing, like why you are there.
Ask one question, such as what brought them along.
Leave comfortably whenever you like. You never have to stay longer than feels okay.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What went better than you expected, even in a small way?
challenges.easierStep: Practise your introduction aloud first, or simply stand near a group and listen.

challenges.title: Make a simple purchase and ask one question
challenges.description: Buy something small and ask the person helping you one simple question, such as where to find an item.
challenges.preparation: Decide on one small thing to buy and one question to ask.
instructions: Go to a shop, cafe, or market.
Ask your question in a calm, clear voice.
Say thank you and finish your purchase.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel, and what did you notice about how it actually went?
challenges.easierStep: Ask your question using a self-checkout help point, or just say thanks to the cashier.

challenges.title: Thank someone who helps you
challenges.description: Say a genuine thank you to someone who does something helpful, like holding a door or serving you.
challenges.preparation: Keep an eye out for a small helpful moment today.
instructions: Notice when someone does something helpful.
Look at them briefly and say thank you.
Notice how the moment feels, then move on.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel, and what did you notice about how it actually went?
challenges.easierStep: Say thank you quietly or with a nod and a smile.

challenges.title: Ask someone to clarify something
challenges.description: When something is unclear, ask a calm question to check you understood, instead of guessing.
challenges.preparation: Think of a recent time you were unsure. Asking for clarity is a normal, useful skill.
instructions: Wait for a natural moment.
Say something like: Could you explain that part again?
Listen, and say thanks for the explanation.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What happened when you asked, and how did the other person respond?
challenges.easierStep: Ask the question in a message or email rather than aloud.

challenges.title: Ask for a recommendation
challenges.description: At a cafe, shop, or library, ask someone what they would recommend.
challenges.preparation: Pick a place where people expect questions, like a bookshop or cafe.
instructions: Choose a calm moment.
Ask: What do you like here?, or: What would you suggest?
Listen to the answer and say thank you, whether or not you take their suggestion.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel, and what did you notice about how it actually went?
challenges.easierStep: Read a staff recommendation card or shelf label instead.

challenges.title: Say what you would like when choosing
challenges.description: When choosing a place to eat or something to watch with a friend, say what you would prefer.
challenges.preparation: Decide ahead of time what you might say, like: I would enjoy pizza tonight.
instructions: Wait until a choice comes up.
State one preference in a friendly tone.
Stay open to what others say too.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel to have a preference heard?
challenges.easierStep: Share a preference in a message, or tell a friend something you like.

challenges.title: Express a preference in a group
challenges.description: Share a simple preference when a group is deciding something, like a meeting time or a place to eat.
challenges.preparation: Pick one small decision where your preference genuinely matters to you.
instructions: Listen to the options first.
Say your preference in one short sentence.
Accept whatever the group decides, and notice how it went.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel, and what did you notice about how it actually went?
challenges.easierStep: Tell just one person in the group your preference beforehand.

challenges.title: Share an opinion respectfully in a group
challenges.description: Offer your view on a topic in a kind, clear way, even when others may see it differently.
challenges.preparation: Choose a low-stakes topic. Plan one sentence beginning with: I think... or: For me...
instructions: Listen to at least one other view.
Share your opinion in one or two sentences.
If someone disagrees, you can say: Thanks, that is a fair point.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you do even though it felt difficult?
challenges.easierStep: Write your opinion down first, or share it with one trusted person.

challenges.title: Practise saying I would prefer... aloud
challenges.description: Rehearse assertive, polite phrases on your own so they feel more familiar.
challenges.preparation: Find a private spot. Choose two or three phrases such as: I would prefer...
instructions: Say each phrase aloud, slowly.
Try it with a calm voice, then a warm voice.
Notice which one feels most like you.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: Which phrase felt most natural, and where might you use it?
challenges.easierStep: Say the phrase quietly or write it down.

challenges.title: Decline something small, politely
challenges.description: Say no to a small offer or request in a kind, clear way.
challenges.preparation: Choose something small, such as turning down an extra at a shop or a minor favour.
instructions: Pause and check what you actually want.
Say something like: No thank you, I am fine.
You do not have to over-explain.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What was it like to say no kindly?
challenges.easierStep: Practise the phrase aloud alone first.

challenges.title: Make a reasonable request
challenges.description: Ask for something fair, like a quieter table, a deadline change, or a bit of help.
challenges.preparation: Be clear about what you want and why it is reasonable. Plan one calm sentence.
instructions: Choose a calm moment.
State your request simply: Would it be possible to...?
Listen to the answer. A no is information, not a verdict on you.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What would you tell a friend who did this?
challenges.easierStep: Make the request in writing, or rehearse it aloud first.

challenges.title: Practise introducing yourself aloud
challenges.description: Say a short introduction out loud on your own: your name and one thing about you.
challenges.preparation: Think of one friendly sentence about yourself.
instructions: Stand or sit comfortably.
Say your introduction aloud twice.
Adjust anything that feels unnatural.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What would you change, and what already sounds good?
challenges.easierStep: Say it in a whisper, or write it down first.

challenges.title: Record a one-minute talk
challenges.description: Record yourself speaking for about a minute on a topic you like, then listen back kindly.
challenges.preparation: Pick a simple topic like a favourite place. Recordings stay on your device unless you share them.
instructions: Take a few slow breaths.
Record yourself talking for about a minute.
Listen back and name two things that went fine.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you notice that you liked?
challenges.easierStep: Record just 20 seconds.

challenges.title: Give a short presentation
challenges.description: Share a few minutes of prepared content with a small, friendly audience.
challenges.preparation: Prepare three simple points. Practise aloud once or twice. Choose a supportive audience.
instructions: Breathe slowly before you begin.
Share your three points at your own pace.
Pausing is fine. Finish with a simple thank you.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you learn, and what would you try next time?
challenges.easierStep: Present to one friend, or practise aloud alone.

challenges.title: Ask a colleague or classmate a simple question
challenges.description: Ask someone nearby a practical question, like how something works or when something is due.
challenges.preparation: Think of one real, small question you have.
instructions: Pick a calm moment.
Ask your question simply.
Say thanks for the answer.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel, and what did you notice about how it actually went?
challenges.easierStep: Send the question as a message.

challenges.title: Give someone a genuine compliment
challenges.description: Offer a sincere, specific compliment when it feels natural and appropriate.
challenges.preparation: Notice something you truly appreciate, like effort or a helpful habit.
instructions: Choose something honest and specific.
Say it briefly and kindly.
Let them respond however they like.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel to give it, and how did it land?
challenges.easierStep: Write the compliment in a message or card.

challenges.title: Contribute one idea in a meeting or class
challenges.description: Share one idea, question, or comment in a group setting.
challenges.preparation: Jot down one idea before the session. A question counts too.
instructions: Listen for a natural opening.
Say your idea in one or two sentences.
Notice that you did it, whatever the response.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you do even though it felt hard?
challenges.easierStep: Send your idea by chat or after the meeting.

challenges.title: Attend a gathering and start one conversation
challenges.description: Go to a social event you feel okay about and begin one conversation.
challenges.preparation: Choose a friendly event. Plan one opener and an easy way to leave when you are ready.
instructions: Arrive when you feel ready.
Start one conversation using your opener.
Leave when you choose. Even a short visit counts.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What went better than you expected?
challenges.easierStep: Attend for just ten minutes, or go with someone you trust.

challenges.title: Write down three things you handled well
challenges.description: Note three things from this week that you did well, however small.
challenges.preparation: Grab a pen or open a note.
instructions: Think back over the last few days.
Write down three things you handled okay or well.
Read them once, slowly.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What do these say about the effort you are putting in?
challenges.easierStep: Write down just one.

challenges.title: Swap one harsh thought for a kinder one
challenges.description: Notice a critical thought and rewrite it as you would for a friend.
challenges.preparation: Think of a recent moment you judged yourself about.
instructions: Write the harsh thought exactly as it sounds.
Ask: What would I say to a friend?
Write a kinder, realistic version.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How does the kinder version feel compared to the first?
challenges.easierStep: Just notice the harsh thought and name it, without rewriting it.

challenges.title: Do one slightly uncomfortable thing
challenges.description: Choose a small action that stretches you a little, and do it at your own pace.
challenges.preparation: Choose something only mildly uncomfortable that is safe and your own choice.
instructions: Name the action in one sentence.
Take one slow breath.
Do it, then notice how you feel afterwards.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you do even though it felt difficult?
challenges.easierStep: Pick an even smaller version.

challenges.title: Let a pause last three breaths
challenges.description: Practise letting a quiet moment be okay instead of rushing to fill it.
challenges.preparation: Pick a conversation or practise alone.
instructions: When a pause happens, take one slow breath.
Count three breaths if that is comfortable.
Resume with a simple comment or question.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What happened when you let the pause be?
challenges.easierStep: Practise on your own, simply sitting through ten seconds of quiet.

challenges.title: Ask someone to repeat something
challenges.description: If you miss something, ask kindly for it to be repeated.
challenges.preparation: Remember that asking someone to repeat is very ordinary.
instructions: Wait for a natural moment.
Say: Sorry, could you say that again?
Thank them and carry on.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel, and what did you notice about how it actually went?
challenges.easierStep: Practise the phrase aloud alone.

challenges.title: Recover from a small slip kindly
challenges.description: If you stumble over words or make a small mistake, practise a light recovery.
challenges.preparation: Pick a recovery phrase, like: Let me try that again.
instructions: Pause for a breath.
Say your recovery phrase.
Continue without apologising repeatedly.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: What did you notice about how others responded?
challenges.easierStep: Practise the phrase aloud alone.

challenges.title: End a conversation politely
challenges.description: Practise wrapping up a chat in a friendly, clear way.
challenges.preparation: Choose a closing phrase, like: It was nice talking, I am going to head off.
instructions: Wait for a natural pause.
Say your closing phrase with a smile.
Say goodbye and go.
challenges.reflectionPrompt: How did it feel to close the conversation kindly?
challenges.easierStep: Practise the phrase aloud alone.
